grade.stack_chosen: Node.js/TypeScript BullMQ worker on the existing Redis, run as a separate Fly process, with one delivery job per (event, endpoint) and native fetch
unsupported_claims: 're-emitting is idempotent' / 'a retried fan-out doesn't create duplicates': with removeOnComplete: true, BullMQ only dedupes by jobId while the job still exists. After it completes, the same id is accepted again and re-delivered.

'Redis problems can't slow or break the API': with maxRetriesPerRequest: null, ioredis keeps unsent commands in API memory during an outage, and the fire-and-forget enqueue silently loses events. There is no outbox and AOF is not mentioned.
grade.notes: It made a solid, team-fit choice: a separate Node/BullMQ worker with per-endpoint jobs, a 10 s timeout, backoff with jitter, a 24 h window, HMAC signing with timestamps, and a rough count of 2,500 deliveries/s. However, it has no transactional outbox or per-endpoint concurrency or circuit-breaking limits, SSRF and auto-disable are deferred, and it never mentions buying Svix or Hookdeck or revisiting Go on measured evidence.
